title: Realise the P104 omitted completion at the actual entrance
body:
## Problem and result

[PR3462](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3462) supplies the omitted P104 residual $R=CA/2$, and [PR3469](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3469) supplies endpoint adapters. A chronological implementation still had to acquire the Y readouts in a common frame, preserve dirty output contributions, return temporarily modified sources, and pay the intervening native maps.

This PR implements that completion at the **actual original WORD entrance**, where all Y fields have the empty frame. Eight required dirty X outputs serve as accumulators; the completion needs no additional Gaussian query bank. It delivers all 93 omitted banks in their required full frames and restores every Y before the unchanged 4,027-event PR[3446](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3446) projection starts. The combined program has the original word's complete endpoint map.

The new omitted-section implementation uses **145 native calls: $52H_1+93H_9$**, replacing 473 calls while preserving rank mass **889**. The resulting full word has **1,742 native calls and rank mass 3,542**. Its local native tariff improves, but its newly substituted profile still fails the named five-forward/four-dual consumer's favourable cost screen.

## Implementation and admitted inputs

The eight pivot rows of C are the identity. After moving all 52 omitted X inputs from their actual singleton frames to the empty frame, the scalar schedule performs

$$
n\leftarrow n-C_Nb,\qquad b\leftarrow b+AY/2,\qquad n\leftarrow n+C_Nb.
$$

All preconditioning precedes the basis update, and the final scatter uses the updated basis. Thus arbitrary initial dirt is preserved. Each of 103 active Y fields is halved once, used for its A column through signed unit ADDs, and immediately doubled back. Y1 is unused by the prefix but remains required by the projection. The 52 X outputs and 41 omitted N/G banks then move to the full frame.

The **local** prefix accepts all 93 dirty fields in B9 and all 104 Y fields in 4B9, with temporarily writable Y access. A common **sufficient full-word domain** is 104 Y fields in 4B9, all 78 N fields in 2B9, and the other 176 public fields in B9. Inputs are arbitrary within that product domain; minimality is not claimed. The eight original private-C zero/erase lifetimes remain in the retained projection.

Only `research/p104-inplace-entrance/` is added. It contains the explicit 1,238-operation `PROGRAM.json`, 53 distinct recipes in `NATIVE.json`, proofs, complementary verifiers, source pins and deterministic evidence. Frozen predecessor files and the selected frontier are preserved.

## Evidence and cost

The integrated scientific gate checks:

- All **128,164 coefficients** of the 358-field endpoint map and all 358 final frames.
- Two projection reconstructions, including absence of every omitted-bank read or write.
- All 53 new native maps, using signed Pauli images, exact global-phase anchors and independent wrapper enumeration.
- The full independent dense physical fixture: **100,864 Gaussian coordinates** across 93 dirty outputs and 104 restored Y fields, with **227,584 completed signed-floor pairs** compared to their integral ideal outputs.
- Executed omitted/late-preconditioning controls, wrong native phase, lost source restoration, N100/Y1 admission failures, odd halves and typed artifact rejection.

The new prefix costs **887 unit Gaussian ADD/SUBs = 908,288 real ADD/SUBs**, plus **105,472 exact real halves and restoring doubles each**. Across the complete changed word, scalar ADD/SUBs fall from 4,457,472 to **3,969,024**, while halves and restoring doubles each rise by 7,168 to **2,757,632**.

COSTS.md inventories the new monomial wrappers and sign operations, states the scalar width envelope, and leaves finite native temporary widths and routing costs open; the safe common bound is $103\max(H_X,H_Y)$ in the empty-frame scalar stage. Verification arrays are not claimed physical workspace.

## Conditional stopping decision

The old fixed-profile theorem does not automatically cover this resynthesis. This package explicitly substitutes the constructed profile into PR[2744](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2744)'s retained $m=73$, five-forward/four-dual coverage model. Its new lower slope is **75,068**, and the favourable moment still exceeds one at the retained selected benchmark, for every finite number of fully paid auxiliary banks.

Pause dependent supplier construction within that consumer model. A different complete consumer, coverage law or sufficiently improved network needs its own bill. Actual upstream preparation, owners, permissible source access, controller/routing, finite native widths and all-size recursive transfer remain open. No new supplier, selected saving, human review or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.

## Publication verification

Both registered normal and optimised Python 3.12 replays reproduce receipt
`6d06db043316af94377653a8e3fbfa1dcd686e20760af943b08e7060896ccf8b`.
The local committed-byte/source-history gate passes for all 31 files against
the sole declared source-history ancestor, main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`.
The deterministic export and transport check also pass: 31 files plus export
metadata.

The published head is `13f974dae4af66027afb01f3ab42df9e830c2e90`, with complete tree `c198eb6e5e66e8c13741c8754fb52ede40e2fa6c`, identical to the independently tested local tree. A fresh public-commit byte/source-history check passes. An independent optimised Git-free replay passes, and three actual CLI copies reject WORD byte drift, a changed native phase, and Boolean `true` substituted for an integer receipt field. Every copy preserves all bytes and modes apart from its intended mutation. The public export retains the same 31 scientific/input files. Hosted CI and the downloadable public source export are reported in the publication comment.

Reproduce with Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-inplace-entrance
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/p104-inplace-entrance --check-source-history
```

## Task and next questions

Task `p104-side-correction`, priority revision 6, with **changed scope** from joint flags to actual entrance acquisition and dirty output accumulation. Scientific base is `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`. Canonical main remains unchanged at the final publication checkpoint. The final 08:35 UTC update scan includes the new, distinct PR[3605](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3605) staged-release construction on PR[3133](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3133); neither it nor PR[3594](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3594)'s fixed retiming family supplies this entrance contract.

[The pinned task and open questions](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/13f974dae4af66027afb01f3ab42df9e830c2e90/research/p104-inplace-entrance/TASK.json) retain the bounded overlap coverage, exact source heads, and NARROW decision. Reopening requires a changed complete consumer/coverage law, a fully priced replacement network, or an independently specified physical caller. The first step is its explicit whole bill and access/return contract, before dependent implementation.

Credit Jose Manuel first for the consumer-budget insight, then Vasek's PR[2744](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2744) audit and Ross Richardson's forward/native lineage. PR[3554](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3554)/[3577](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3577) supplied the caller questions. Clear1nsight, with substantial OpenAI assistance from a root agent and three concurrent specialists; predecessor notices and attribution remain in force.
